units.title: Greek Inventors
units.blurb: Archimedes of Syracuse and Hero of Alexandria: levers, floating bodies, steam and clever machines.

units.title: Light and Experiment
units.blurb: Ibn al-Haytham in Cairo, who tested ideas about light and sight in a darkened room.

topics.title: Archimedes: The Lever and the Crown
topics.short: A Greek of Syracuse (c. 287–212 BC) who proved the law of the lever, worked out why things float, and built machines that astonished his city.
topics.trouble: People treat the Eureka bath story as a known fact; it comes from a Roman writer two centuries later.

topics.title: Hero of Alexandria: Steam, Air and Automatic Machines
topics.short: A teacher in Roman Egypt (about the 1st century AD) who described a spinning steam ball, automatic doors and a coin-operated dispenser.
topics.trouble: People think Hero built a working steam engine for doing work; his aeolipile was a demonstration that did no useful work.

topics.title: Ibn al-Haytham: Light, Sight and the Dark Room
topics.short: A scholar of Basra and Cairo (c. AD 965–c. 1040) whose Book of Optics showed that we see because light enters the eye, and tested it.
topics.trouble: People think the eye sends out rays to see; many ancient thinkers did, and Ibn al-Haytham showed why that fails.
